question: According to Mendel’s Law of Segregation (分離定律), when do the alleles of a gene pair separate from each other?
options: During mitosis / 有絲分裂期間
During gamete formation in meiosis / 減數分裂形成配子期間
During random combinations in fertilization / 受精時的隨機組合期間
During DNA replication in somatic cells / 體細胞進行 DNA 複製期間

question: In the ABO blood group inheritance system, alleles IA and IB are co-dominant (共顯性), while allele i is recessive (隱性).
Why is red-green colour blindness (紅綠色盲), which is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome, significantly more common in males than in females?
options: Males have two Y chromosomes that suppress the normal dominant allele.
The Y chromosome carries a dominant modifier gene for colour blindness.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele will express the characteristic.
Females produce specialized anti-B antibodies in plasma that neutralize the allele.

options: ABO blood groups / ABO 血型

question: Discontinuous variations (不連續變異), such as hand span and foot length, are represented using a bar chart showing a normal distribution curve with a characteristic bell shape.
What are alleles (等位基因)?
options: Different chromosomes found inside the nucleus of a gamete
Alternative forms of the same gene occupying the same gene locus on homologous chromosomes
Identical copies of a chromosome joined at the centromere
Enzymes that control the rate of DNA replication

question: In humans, a father always passes his single X chromosome to all of his daughters and his Y chromosome to all of his sons.
Which statement correctly describes the causes of variation among individuals of the same species?
options: Continuous variation is controlled only by a single gene and is unaffected by the environment.

Discontinuous variation shows a continuous range of intermediate phenotypes between two extremes.

[PEDIGREE & GENETIC ANALYSIS] In a family pedigree tracing hair patterns, two parents with curly hair have an offspring with straight hair. 1) Deduce which allele is dominant and explain your reasoning. 2) If these curly-haired parents have another child, calculate the theoretical probability that the child will have straight hair.
rubric: To score full points, the response must demonstrate structural mastery: 1) The allele for curly hair is dominant. Because both parents exhibit curly hair but produce a straight-haired child, the parents must be heterozygous. Under heterozygous conditions, only the dominant allele expresses itself physically, while the recessive allele is masked. 2) The theoretical probability of having a straight-haired child (homozygous recessive) from a standard heterozygous monohybrid cross (Aa x Aa) is 1/4 or 25%.
